name: Licensing, usage rights and releases
one_line: Refused as a creative template: executed grants and releases are legal instruments, royalty records are finance records, and the creative work is their subject rather than a distinct filing schema.
refuse_reason: This label joins three different record functions without a creative-specific field set: an executed licence, assignment, model release, property release or location release is an instrument that activates the legal safety schema from party recitals, operative grant/consent language and execution evidence; a royalty statement, usage report or payment advice activates finance from issuer, period and transaction structure; and the licensed photograph, track, illustration, font or footage remains creative work. Rights scope, territory, term, exclusivity, media and licensor/licensee roles would be useful facts, but the creative schema declares no fields and this placeholder may not mint them. More importantly, those facts describe the legal grant, not the creative work as such. A distinct creative template would therefore duplicate legal/finance detection and organize by proposed fields unavailable to its schema. Coverage routes by active schema to legal or finance, with standalone unactivated files falling through to Protected Records, Independent Records, Receipts and Confirmations, Review Later, Reference Clips, or Unsupported or Encrypted.

never_alone: the word licence, license, rights, release, royalty, usage or consent alone; each occurs in legal instruments, finance reports, software notices, stock-asset receipts and ordinary prose
a creative-work title, asset identifier, thumbnail, filename or embedded preview; it identifies subject matter but does not prove that rights were granted
a person or organization name read as licensor, licensee, releasor, photographer, agency or client without a labelled party role or operative clause
a signature image, signed suffix or e-signature platform filename without the instrument's party and grant structure
a money amount without a labelled royalty, usage, sales, withholding or payment-period structure
a territory name or date range without a labelled grant context; either may describe production, publication, travel or accounting
an extension or SOURCE_TYPE alone, including PDF, DOCX, image, spreadsheet, email and archive
membership in a creative project folder or delivery archive; neighbourhood may support reviewable grouping but may not copy a rights fact onto the file

template.why: Empty because the node is refused. The apparent order — creative work or agreement, then grant type, territory, term and exploitation medium — depends entirely on rights fields that the creative schema does not declare. Using project, client, work title, licensor or licensee instead would turn subject names and party roles into an unlicensed creative schema. The legal or finance schema should supply any eventual dimensions after its own field decision; residual placement remains available when neither activates.

collides_with.signal: Same bytes: Campaign-photography-usage-licence-executed.pdf and Model Release - Jordan Lee - signed.pdf. Party recitals, operative grant or consent clauses and execution blocks support legal; a work title, thumbnail, campaign name or creative-project neighbourhood supports only the subject relationship and cannot activate a separate creative rights template. On the reverse boundary, a creative brief or asset master naming usage goals but containing no operative grant remains creative and does not activate legal.

Same bytes: Q2 2026 Sound Recording Royalty Statement.xlsx and Getty Images licence receipt 8842103.pdf. Issuer, reporting period, line items, amounts, withholding and payment totals support finance; grant scope and executed party obligations support legal. The word royalty or licence appears on both and discriminates neither. On the reverse boundary, a finance payment record cannot establish copyright ownership or the full scope of permitted exploitation.

A client statement of work may contain deliverables, fees and a rights clause, while an executed usage licence may name the same client and campaign. Engagement scope, review rounds and delivery obligations support client-engagement; an operative grant specifying permitted use supports legal. A client name and project title support neither side alone, and the rights clause remains legal evidence rather than a new creative dimension.

A handoff packet may include masters, checksums, delivery manifests and a copy of the licence. Asset inventory, formats, transfer confirmation and checksum structure support deliverable-handoff; party recitals, grant language and execution support legal. Delivery of bytes does not itself transfer copyright or establish permission to exploit them, while a licence does not prove that deliverables were actually handed off.

Same bytes: a passport scan included beside model releases. A filename or folder saying model release does not turn the scan into rights evidence. Travel-document labels, bearer fields and machine-readable structure support identity and immediate protection; consent and execution blocks support legal. On the reverse boundary, a signed model release names a person but does not thereby become an identity document.

sensitivity_why: Executed licences and releases expose names, signatures, contact details, negotiated commercial terms, likeness consents and sometimes identity attachments. Royalty statements expose income, tax withholding and account information. Protection must precede any model path or placement proposal. This sensitivity reinforces legal/finance routing but is not enough to create a creative template.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-CLR-1: Should a later legal-schema decision add rights-grant fields such as grant scope, exploitation medium, territory, term, exclusivity and party roles, or should those remain searchable extracted clauses only? NJ-CLR-2: Should royalty statements with work-level exploitation rows activate only finance, or co-activate a future rights catalogue once legal has fields? NJ-CLR-3: Should an informal, unexecuted email grant surface as possible legal material under local review, or remain Review Later until an instrument or explicit user confirmation exists? None of these questions rescues this creative node today: the creative schema declares no fields, and work titles plus licensor/licensee roles are values or relationships rather than a creative-specific template.
